text:
Assistant B is better. It is more concise, as the user asked, and it includes a subject line. It uses a numbered list of arguments, offers personal support ("I'll be there to support you every step of the way"), and acknowledges the friend's introversion with empathy. Its weaknesses are that it addresses objections only lightly and doesn't say what the event is.

Assistant A is longer and more generic. It has no subject line and its tone is more formal. It does address objections more explicitly, saying everyone in the audience is supportive, that the friend is knowledgeable, and that practice makes it easier. But it offers no personal support and no concrete details, and its length works against the "concise" instruction.

Overall, B fits the request better on conciseness and personal connection, while A is slightly stronger on objection handling.

[[B]]
